status: Working draft · based on supplied guide · not independently verified

about.intro: The Social Protection Services Support Guide is a practical resource for healthcare workers, patients, caregivers, and families seeking information on social protection services in Jamaica. It brings together programmes, agencies, referral points, and contact information to help people identify a possible service and take the next step.
about.why: Health outcomes can be affected by income, food security, housing, disability, family stability, education, safety, and access to community support. This guide is intended to help connect clinical care with relevant social protection services.
about.audience: Healthcare workers can use the guide to screen for social needs, support discharge planning, make informed referrals, and guide patients toward services. Patients and caregivers can use it to explore possible assistance, where to start, and what information may be requested.
how: Start with the overview to understand agencies and types of support.
Compare programme profiles, target groups, benefits, and referral options.
Use the Decision Guide to connect a situation with a possible programme or agency.
Use the Contact Directory to confirm current requirements, locations, forms, and application steps.
about.disclaimer: This guide does not replace official agency assessments or eligibility decisions. Requirements, benefits, and contact details may change. Confirm current information directly with the responsible ministry, agency, medical social work department, or parish office before applying or advising someone.

referralSteps: Ask respectful questions about what is affecting care or wellbeing. Possible needs include food, medication, transport, housing, safety, income, disability support, school attendance, caregiving, mental health, or help after an emergency.

If there is immediate danger, serious medical distress, suspected abuse, suicidal thoughts, severe neglect, or a child-protection concern, treat it as urgent. Follow facility emergency and safeguarding procedures first, then connect with the appropriate clinician, social worker, hotline, police, child-protection or crisis-response service.
Match the person to a service

Use the programme profiles, Decision Guide, and Contact Directory to identify a suitable starting point. When needs overlap, prioritise immediate safety, health, and basic needs before longer-term support.

Explain the purpose and what the service may ask for. Depending on the programme, useful documents may include identification, TRN, proof of address, clinic card, prescription, medical letter, discharge summary, birth certificate, school information, disability documentation, or evidence of an emergency.
Make a warm referral where possible
With the person’s consent, help connect them directly: call the agency, send a referral note, link to a medical social worker, confirm office hours, or explain the next step.
Record the need, referral, agency/contact, and urgent concerns in line with facility policy. Where appropriate, check later whether the person accessed the service or needs further support.

programmes.name: PATH
programmes.where: Visit the Office in the Parish where you reside
programmes.bring: Birth Certificates (all members); TRN & National ID (Adults)
programmes.process: Interview completed → household scored → home visit for verification → approved applicants receive PATH benefits
programmes.support: Conditional cash grants for eligible households’ members; benefits are provided for up to four years before reassessment.

programmes.name: Local Government Assistance
programmes.bring: Valid ID / TRN (if available); Application form Supporting documents (proof of need, bills, etc.)
programmes.process: Visit or call Office → complete relevant section of the form → Assessment/investigation by Poor Relief Officer → Decision communicated to the applicant
programmes.support: Poor relief, emergency assistance, homeless support, institutional care/infirmary placement, meals, housing, or community assistance based on assessed need. Other services

programmes.name: HEART / NSTA
programmes.bring: Application form; TRN; Valid ID / Birth certificate; Email address & mobile number; Academic qualifications; Course-related supporting documents
programmes.process: Complete and submit application → complete any required assessments → documents reviewed → accepted applicants register and start training
programmes.support: Skills training, certification, assessments, and employment-readiness support; course schedules and duration vary by programme.

programmes.name: NHF
programmes.bring: National ID; TRN; Completed form (signed by doctor)
programmes.process: Available online and pharmacies Doctor completes form and sign → patient submits to NHF → receives card → use at pharmacies for subsidised medication and laboratories for subsidised lab tests
programmes.support: NHF card covers all ages with chronic illnesses; diagnostic tests, ECG, ECO, Persons with disabilities (registered with JCPD – double the subsidy Children – double subsidy

programmes.name: NIS
programmes.where: Visit the Office in the Parish where you reside
programmes.bring: TRN; Valid ID; Birth Certificate or Passport; Bank account details; Marriage Certificate or Deed Poll (if applicable), NIS number
programmes.process: Check contributions → apply 4 months before 65th birthdate if retired → submit form and supporting documents → NIS verifies record and claim → if pension approved, payments made to the bank account. Check contributions record periodically. Invalidity insurance Widows Pension
programmes.support: Social insurance for eligible contributors and dependents; payments made by direct deposit.

programmes.name: National Housing Trust (NHT)
programmes.bring: Valid Photo ID, TRN, NIS card, Proof of Income, Land Title/Authorization letter, and NHT Registration number
programmes.process: Visit office for initial assessment → Interview and income verification → Social work field visit (if applying for social housing) → Final approval for grant, 0% rate, or unit allocation
programmes.support: Non-repayable home grants (up to $3.5M);

programmes.name: New Social Housing Programme (NSHP)
programmes.where: • Office of your local Member of Parliament (MP) • Ministry of Economic Growth and Job Creation (MEGJC) • Poor Relief Department of your parish Municipal Corporation
programmes.bring: • Valid Government Photo ID • Tax Registration Number (TRN) & NIS card • Proof of land ownership, registered title, or a notarized letter of legal permission to build on the land • Proof of income / financial status (or affidavit of indigent status)
programmes.process: Submit an application via your local MP or Poor Relief office → Rigorous filtering and verification of living conditions → Case review and field assessment by a social worker/officer → Final selection by the NSHP Project Oversight Committee → Unit construction and formal handover.
programmes.support: Housing solution - ranging from 1 to 3-bedroom detached units or semi-permanent modular structures

programmes.name: Grants (RADA / JBDC)
programmes.where: RADA Parish Office or JBDC Office
programmes.bring: TRN; Business/Farm Registration; Valid ID
programmes.process: Meet advisor → business/farm assessed → may receive training, site visit, or grant approval
programmes.support: Technical advice, training, business development support, farm support, and grant or loan referrals where available, back yard gardening

programmes.name: CHASE / Compassionate Medical Assistance
programmes.where: CHASE application route on CHASE Fund Website or corporate office in Kingston
programmes.bring: Medical report or doctor's letter; Diagnosis, prescription or diagnostic request; Cost estimate/proforma invoice; ID, TRN, and proof of financial need
programmes.process: Doctor/social worker confirms need → application and supporting documents submitted → case reviewed → approved funds or services are paid to provider or coordinated through the public system
programmes.support: Case-by-case assistance for specialised surgeries, diagnostics, medication, cancer care, kidney treatment and other urgent or severe medical needs.

programmes.name: MOHW Compassionate Fund Programme
programmes.where: MOHW Enabling Environment in Health and Client Services Division in Kingston, Public hospital or health facility Social Work Department under the relevant Regional Health Authority
programmes.bring: Application form, ID, TRN, Medical report or doctor's letter; prescription (if applicable, Proforma invoice/Quotation, Pre-authorised letter (if insured), Birth certificate (if minor), Job letter (if employed), Character reference, and Written letter of request
programmes.process: Doctor confirms need → application and supporting documents submitted → case reviewed → applicant receives MOHW commitment letter of approved amount → applicant receives service → service provider submits signed commitment letter, and invoice to MOHW
programmes.support: Case-by-case assistance for specialised surgeries, medication, cancer care, device, kidney treatment, and other urgent or severe medical needs.

programmes.name: RHA Diagnostic Support
programmes.where: Public hospital or health facility under the relevant Regional Health Authority
programmes.bring: Public hospital registration; Doctor's referral or diagnostic request; Patient ID and clinic/hospital information
programmes.process: Public doctor issues request → hospital schedules in-house test or outsourcing referral → patient receives approved diagnostic service at no out-of-pocket cost where covered
programmes.support: CT scans, MRIs, ultrasounds, and other approved diagnostic tests/services for public patients.

programmes.name: NCDA Support
programmes.where: NCDA office, helpline, or community clinic
programmes.bring: Basic personal information; Referral note if available; Health or social history relevant to treatment
programmes.process: Contact NCDA → screening or assessment → counselling, community clinic appointment or referral → follow-up support as needed
programmes.support: Confidential counselling, prevention, drug testing, treatment referral, outreach, and psychosocial support.

programmes.name: Child Protection and Family Services Agency (CPFSA)
programmes.where: Nearest CPFSA Parish Office or Regional Office
programmes.bring: Child's birth certificate, if available; Parent's or guardian's identification; Relevant medical, school or other supporting documents, if applicable; Details of the concern or incident being reported
programmes.process: Report concern or request assistance → intake and assessment → investigation or referral, as appropriate → intervention and follow-up.
programmes.support: Child abuse, neglect and abandonment investigations, Counselling and family support, Foster care and adoption services, Residential care and protection, Court and child welfare services

programmes.name: Victim Services Branch
programmes.where: Ministry of Justice Victim Services office or helpline
programmes.bring: Basic personal information; Police report or case reference if available; Court date or referral information if applicable
programmes.process: Contact VSB → needs assessment → counselling, court support, referral or crisis response arranged → follow-up support provided
programmes.support: Free confidential counselling, emotional support, court orientation, referral and victim-sensitive services.

programmes.name: Women's Centre Programme for Adolescent Mothers
programmes.where: Women's Centre main centre, outreach station, school, clinic, or hospital referral
programmes.bring: Birth certificate or ID if available; School information; Clinic card or pregnancy-related referral if available
programmes.process: Referral or walk-in → intake and counselling → education support during pregnancy → reintegration planning after birth
programmes.support: Continuing education, counselling, parenting guidance and reintegration support for adolescent mothers.

programmes.name: Senior Citizen Services / Meals on Wheels
programmes.where: National Council for Senior Citizens, MLSS parish office, health centre, or community referral point
programmes.bring: Valid ID or birth certificate; TRN if available; Proof of address and need
programmes.process: Referral or application → needs assessment → programme match or referral → follow-up by senior services or parish office
programmes.support: Meals, referrals, social support, advocacy and senior-focused welfare assistance where available.

programmes.name: Bureau of Gender Affairs Services
programmes.where: GBV helpline, Ministry of Culture, Gender, Entertainment and Sport, police domestic violence intervention centre, or referral partner
programmes.bring: Basic personal information if safe to provide; Incident details or referral note if available; Immediate safety concerns and preferred safe contact method
programmes.process: Call or text for support → trained social worker or counsellor assesses safety and need → referral made for counselling, shelter, police, victim services, legal aid or welfare support → follow-up arranged where safe
programmes.support: Gender-based violence response, domestic violence support, psychosocial counselling, public education, gender equality training and referral coordination.

documents.requirements: Must generally be 18+ and a Jamaican citizen ordinarily resident in Jamaica; bring birth certificate/proof of age if recently turned 18. Other personal information is collected during registration.
documents.process: 1. Visit an EOJ constituency office. 2. Complete Registration Record Card. 3. Photo and fingerprints are taken. 4. EOJ verifies your residence. 5. Information is processed. 6. Once registered and the Voters' List is published, collect your Voter ID.

documents.where: Any commercial bank or its online banking platform.
documents.requirements: Valid government-issued photo ID (e.g., passport, driver's license or voter ID); Tax Registration Number (TRN); Proof of residential address (e.g., utility bill or bank statement); Proof of income or source of funds (e.g., job letter or payslip); Minimum opening deposit, if required
documents.process: 1. Choose a bank and account type. 2.Gather the required documents. 3.Complete the application online or at a branch. 3.Submit documents for verification. 4.Make the required opening deposit. 5.Receive your account details and debit card, if applicable
documents.cost: Varies by bank and account type. Minimum opening deposits may apply.

documents.requirements: Birth Certificate/Citizenship Certificate; 2 identical photos; government ID; certified application; name-change documents where applicable
documents.process: 1. Complete passport application. 2. Get application/photos certified. 3. Gather birth certificate, ID and photos. 4. Submit application to PICA. 5. Pay fee. 6. Collect passport when ready..
documents.cost: Contact the entity to confirm the cost based on the service

documents.requirements: Provisional license; birth certificate/proof of age; TRN; medical certificate; photographs; required tests
documents.process: 1. Get learner's/provisional license. 2. Pass Road Code Test. 3. Take driving lessons. 4. Book and complete driving test. 5. Pass yard and road tests. 6. Pay applicable fee. 7. Receive driver's licence.
documents.cost: Contact the entity to confirm the cost based on the service
